Ps II 264, 28 (pāḷiṃ vā aṭṭhakathaṃ vā dhammakathābandhaṃ vā ~aṃ vā na sikkhāpenti, Ce, Ee so; Be, Se guyha-; Ps-ṭ [ Be ] II 198, 17 : saccasattapaṭisandhipaccayākārapaṭisaṃyuttaṃ suññatādīpanaṃ guyhaganthaṃ) = Mp V 97, 1 ( Ce so; Be, Ee, Se guḷha-); — gūḷha-paṭicchanna, mfn. , 1. undetected and not known about ; Sp 811, 15 (so kira Ajātasattunā rājānaṃ mārāpetvā pi … ~-paṭicchanno va ahosi, Ce so; Be, Ee, Se guḷha-); — 2. having a secret and hidden meaning ; Dhp-a I 402, 19 (~-paṭicchanne dasa ovāde adāsi, Ce, Ee so; Se guyha-; Be guyhe paṭicchanne); — gūḷha-purisa, m. , a disguised or secret agent ; Abh 347 (caro ca ~-puriso); — ( iii ) secret, private (ie heterodox) ;? disguised, altered ;? [ S. guhya], 1. (what is) to be covered or concealed; the parts of the body which should be covered, esp. the private parts; (what is) to be kept secret, secret, private; a secret ; Abh 352 (rahassaṃ ~am uccate); 1061 (~aṃ liṅge rahasy api); D III 187, 12 (~aṃ assa ācikkhati); Thī 74 (pilandhanaṃ vidaṃsentī ~aṃ pakāsikaṃ bahuṃ, Be, Ce, Ee so; Se pakāsitaṃ; Thī-a 76, 32 foll. : ūrujaghana-thanadassanādikaṃ guyhaṃ c’ eva pādajānusirādikaṃ pakāsaṃ cā ti …); Ja V 76, 6 (idaṃ amhākaṃ ~aṃ rahassaṃ); 77, 22* (tassāhaṃ akkhiṃ vivariṃ ~am atthaṃ); 81, 16* (thiyā ~aṃ na saṃseyya amittassa ca paṇḍito); 196, 12* (vidaṃsayantī aṅgāni ~aṃ pakāsitāni ca; 196, 16´ : ~aṃ ca rahassaṅgaṃ pakāsitāni ca pākaṭāni mukhahatthādīni); VI 383, 30 (mahāsatto sabbesaṃ pi ~aṃ paccakkhaṃ akāsi); Mil 92, 25 (nav’ ime puggalā mantitaṃ ~aṃ vivaranti na dhārenti); 168, 30 (na mahārāja bhagavā ~aṃ dassesi iddhiyā chāyaṃ dassesi); Spk I 93, 26 (aññesaṃ akathetabbassa pi ~assa kathetabbayuttatāya bhariyā paramā sakhā nāma); — ifc see vattha- ( sv vattha 1 ); — 2. to be hidden in ;? Ja II 174, 7* (puṇṇaṃ nadiṃ yena ca peyyam āhu jātaṃ yavaṃ yena ca ~am āhu, a riddle for kāka; cf 174, 15´ foll. : taṃ [taruṇasassaṃ] hi yadā antopaviṭṭhakākaṃ paṭicchādetuṃ sakkoti tadā guyhatī ti guyhaṃ, kiṃ guyhati, kākaṃ, iti kākassa guyhaṃ kākaguyhan ti taṃ vadamānā kākena guyhavacanassa kāraṇabhūtena guyhan ti vadanti); — see also guyha 2 ; — guyhaṃ pi in Ee at Ja IV 204, 28´ is wr, for guyhasi, or fo r gūhasi ( Be, Ce so ); — ~-ppakāsiya, mfn. , to be concealed and to be revealed; private and public ; Ja VI 230, 13* (mā upagacchuṃ atthesu ~-ppakāsiyesu ca, Be so; Ce, Ee, Se ~-ppākāsiyesu ca); — ~-bhaṇḍaka, n. , the (ornaments of the) covered part of the body ;? Ja V 434, 4 (kaṭiṃ cāleti ~-bhaṇḍakaṃ sañcāleti) ≠ Dhp-a IV 197, 7 ; — ~-manta, m. and mfn. , 1. ( m. ) a secret or private discussion or plan ; Vin IV 159, 26 (rañño antepure abbhantarā ~-mantā bahiddhā sambhedaṃ gacchanti); A III 129, 13 (Mp III 279, 2 : ~-mantā ti guhitabbamantā); Ja V 77, 14* (yo ~-mantaṃ parirakkhaneyyaṃ mohā naro saṃsati); — 2. ( mfn. ) keeping discussions or plans secret ; Ja V 82, 3* (ye ~-mantā avikiṇṇavācā daḷhā sadatthesu narā; 82, 12´ : ~-mantā purisā evarūpā honti attano guyhaṃ attano anto yeva jīrāpenti na aññassa kathentī ti, Be, Ce, Se so; Ee gūḷhamantā purisā … attano gūḷhaṃ …); — fpp ( b ) guhitabba, guyhitabba, gūhitabba, mfn. , Sv 447, 16 (vatthaguyhan ti vatthena guhitabbaṃ aṅgajātaṃ vuccati, Be, Ce, Ee so; Se guyhitabbaṃ) = Ps III 377, 21 ( Be so; Ce, Ee guyhitabbaṃ; Se gūhitabbaṃ); Mp III 279, 2 (guhitabbamantā); — caus. pr. 3 sg. gūhayati , conceals ; Sadd 830, 8 (guha dusa icc etesaṃ dhātūnaṃ saro kvaci dīghattaṃ āpajjate kārite: ~ati dūsayati); — part.pr. gūhaya(t), mfn. , Saddh 189 (bhayena vinimīlento aṅgaṃ aṅge va ~aṃ).

guhaṭṭhakasutta.p: [Guhā+aṭṭhaka+sutta] (na) CL=8 Suttas containing 8 verses taught about the body, Guhaṭṭhaka sutta.
pn:
Guhaṭṭhakasutta. The second Sutta of the Aṭṭhakavagga of the Suttanipāta; it was preached to Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja. He once went to Udakavana in Kosambī, and there the women of King Udena’s palace, who had come to the park with the king, left the king while he slept, and, finding the Elder, sat down and listened to his preaching. The king, awakening, went in search of them, and was angry when he discovered their whereabouts. He questioned Piṇḍola as to the solitude which he professed to seek in the park, but Piṇḍola refusing to answer, the king threatened to set red ants at him. Thereupon Piṇḍola went through the air to the Buddha’s Gandhakuṭi and related the story. The Buddha was reclining on his bed and, in that position, preached this Sutta to the Elder.

A man who clings to the body and to the pleasures of the senses, lives in constant fear. One should therefore cast off greed and cross the flood, unstained by the world (Snp.vv.772-9; Snp-a.ii.514ff).

The Sutta probably derives its name from the fact that, in the first verse, the body is spoken of as a guhā.

It is commented on in the Mahā Niddesa pp.23ff.

guhāsaya.p: [Guhā+si+a] (ti) CL=8 Guhāyaṃ sayatīti guhāsayo. Mahāni.6.]  Living in a cave. (A)who is lie in cave that is the body. (b) who is being in cave that is  Mahābhuta (the four basic properties of matter i.e solidity, fluidity, heat and volatility (commonly described as the four elements of earth, water, fire and air)).
